learningObjectives: Explain what a calculated field is and how the calculation network keeps dependent fields current
Choose among the three App Studio calculation types — Functions, Expressions, and Decision tables — and apply each correctly

studyGuide.sectionTitle: Calculated values and the calculation network

elements.description: A calculation sets a field's value based on one or more other fields (e.g., Total = Quantity × Price). The calculated field is read-only — the system owns it. Calculations update automatically when any input field changes.

elements.text: A Decision table resembles an ordered checklist of combinations: each row tests its configured inputs and supplies an outcome. Overlapping rows need deliberate ordering; an otherwise outcome handles unmatched combinations. It is not a matrix where a single row/column intersection alone selects a cell.

elements.description: Create the calculated field in the Data model of a CASE TYPE or DATA OBJECT, depending on the use case. Configuration includes field name, type (e.g., Currency), and the 'This is a calculated field (read-only)' option.

A calculated field can be the input to another calculation, creating a dependency chain. Pega resolves the chain in the correct order — downstream fields update automatically when upstream inputs change.

elements.caption: Calculated outputs can feed further calculations. The configured dependency network updates relevant dependent values; it is not a guarantee for unrelated fields or unmodeled dependencies.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: The three App Studio calculation types

elements.description: The basic aggregate Function choices operate over list relationships for Decimal, Currency and Integer fields. The reviewed source identifies Sum of, Average of, Maximum of and Minimum of; do not confuse these choices with every callable function in an expression.

An expression calculates a field value from a combination of fields, functions, and data relationships. Reference fields with the dot operator (.FieldName). Expressions are evaluated at runtime whenever their inputs change.

Assembles a string by joining field references and static text with '+'. Example: "Appraiser " + .AppraiserID + " appraised " + .ItemName + " at " + .AppraisedAmount + ".". Field references are replaced with live values at runtime.

A Decision table maps configured property or expression tests to results. In the standard evaluation described by the topic, test rows from the top; return the first row whose conditions all match, or the configured otherwise result. Numeric tests can use comparisons and ranges; overlapping conditions make ordering significant.

Only applications based on CONSTELLATION support the creation of CUSTOM decision tables directly in App Studio. In non-Constellation apps, the Dev Studio decision table (marked as a relevant record) is how you make the logic available to App Studio.

elements.title: Pick the calculation type

elements.caption: Functions, Expressions and Decision tables are the reviewed calculation choices. Default Value is not a replacement for Functions in this list.

examPitfalls.title: Three calculation types, not four
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The reviewed Calculated values source describes Functions, Expressions and Decision tables. Do not turn the historical terminology into a claim about every platform version or every kind of decision Rule.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Choose the aggregate option for a list, an expression for a formula and a table for condition-to-result combinations.

examPitfalls.title: Functions iterate over a list
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Functions (Sum/Average/Maximum/Minimum of) operate over items in a data relationship and are supported only for Decimal, Currency, and Integer fields.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use a Function when the value aggregates a list of instances; use an Expression for a formula across named fields.

examPitfalls.title: Expression field-type limits
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The reviewed source excludes Email, Phone and Picklist from expression-calculated Simple fields. Do not substitute an incomplete list such as Text, Integer, Double, Date and Boolean or confuse input relationships with output type.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Don't expect an expression to compute Email, Phone, or Picklist fields.

examPitfalls.title: Concatenation is for text
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Concatenation joins field references and static text (in quotes) with '+' to build a string — it is a text expression, not numeric math.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Use concatenation to assemble comments/labels; use math operators for numeric values.

examPitfalls.title: Reuse a Dev Studio table = relevant record
examPitfalls.trapDescription: To reference a decision table built in Dev Studio from App Studio, you must mark it as a relevant record.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Mark the Dev Studio decision table as a relevant record so Citizen Developers can use it in App Studio.

examPitfalls.title: Custom App Studio tables need Constellation
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question asks whether custom Decision Tables can be created and managed in App Studio for Traditional UI applications. Candidates say yes. App Studio's Decision Table management (custom tables) requires Constellation UI — Traditional UI applications must use Dev Studio for Decision Tables.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: On non-Constellation apps, build the table in Dev Studio (relevant record) and reference it.

examPitfalls.title: Calculated fields are read-only and networked
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A calculated field is read-only and recalculates whenever an input changes; Pega's calculation network cascades updates to all dependent calculated fields.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: In the configured calculated-field UI, users do not manually type the derived output. Test the input/dependency configuration rather than assuming every field participates automatically.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Business Architect asks an SA to explain how Pega automatically computes field values that depend on other fields — for example, a total invoice amount derived from line items. What is a calculated field in Pega Platform?

options.text: A field whose value is set automatically from one or more input fields and recalculates whenever an input changes
A free-text field the user types into and then locks manually
A field that stores the result of a Service-Level Agreement timer
A field used only to route assignments to a Work Queue

practiceQuiz.hint: Calculated fields derive their value from inputs and recalculate automatically on change.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A calculation expresses a relationship between fields, setting a calculated field's value from input fields; it recalculates whenever an input updates and is read-only. B, C, and D do not describe a calculated field.

optionExplanations.A: The configured calculation derives a value from its inputs and participates in dependency updates, unlike an arbitrary manually edited field.
optionExplanations.B: Manual free-text entry followed by locking does not define a calculation relationship between input and output fields.
optionExplanations.C: An SLA timer is a timing mechanism, not the definition of every field whose value is derived by a calculation.
optionExplanations.D: Routing may use data, but a routing-only field does not define the calculation relationship asked about here.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is reviewing the options available for configuring Calculated Value fields in App Studio and a junior developer asks what types of calculation logic are supported. Which three calculation types does App Studio provide when configuring a Calculated Value field?

options.text: Functions, Expressions, and Decision tables
Expressions, Decision tables, and Decision trees
Functions, When conditions, and Decision trees
Data transforms, Activities, and Expressions

practiceQuiz.hint: Calculated fields are sourced from Functions, Expressions, or Decision tables in the Data Model.
practiceQuiz.rationale: App Studio allows three calculation types: Functions, Expressions, and Decision tables. The other options mix in items (Decision trees, When conditions, Data transforms, Activities) that are not the App Studio calculation types.

optionExplanations.A: These are the three approaches described in the reviewed calculation source; their purposes differ between aggregation, formula and condition mapping.
optionExplanations.B: Decision trees replace Functions in this option and are not the three named App Studio calculation approaches.
optionExplanations.C: When conditions and Decision trees are not the named calculation choices in this reviewed configuration list.
optionExplanations.D: Data Transforms and Activities are different Rule mechanisms, not replacements for the listed aggregate and table calculation choices.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What do Functions iterate over, and which field types do they support?

options.text: They iterate over items in a data relationship (a list) and support Decimal, Currency, and Integer field types
They iterate over rows of a Decision table and support Text and Date types
They iterate over Stages in a Case and support any field type
They iterate over Access Roles and support Boolean fields only

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall what data structure Functions iterate over and which numeric field types they support.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Functions iterate over items in a data relationship and are supported for Decimal, Currency, and Integer field types. The other options misstate both what they iterate over and the supported types.

optionExplanations.A: The source describes numeric aggregate choices over items in a relationship list, matching both structure and output types here.
optionExplanations.B: Decision-table rows are conditional combinations, not the list relationship over which these numeric aggregates iterate.
optionExplanations.C: Case Stages are lifecycle configuration, not the collection of numeric property values used by these aggregate choices.
optionExplanations.D: Access Roles express security context; iterating roles is not the described numeric relationship aggregation mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Each shopping-cart line already has a calculated cost including its quantity. Which aggregate function produces the order total from those line costs?

options.text: Sum of — adds all items in the specified property instances
Average of — calculates the average value of all instances
Maximum of — determines the largest value of all instances
Minimum of — determines the smallest value of all instances

practiceQuiz.hint: Which calculation function adds all values in a list of property instances to produce a running total?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Sum of adds all items in the specified property instances — exactly what an order total needs. Average of, Maximum of, and Minimum of compute the average, largest, and smallest values respectively.

optionExplanations.A: Adding each already calculated line cost produces the order total; quantity is included at the line level in this scenario.
optionExplanations.B: The mean line cost is not the combined price of all ordered lines; averaging answers a different question.
optionExplanations.C: The largest line cost ignores the other lines and therefore cannot represent their combined order total.
optionExplanations.D: The smallest line cost ignores the other lines and therefore cannot represent their combined order total.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Each eligible promotional discount has a comparable numeric monetary value. Which function selects the largest value from that list?

options.text: Maximum of — determines the largest value among the discounts
Minimum of — determines the smallest value among the discounts
Sum of — adds all the discounts together
Average of — averages the discounts

practiceQuiz.hint: Which calculation function returns the single largest value from a list of property instances?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Maximum of determines the largest value in the list, which is the most valuable discount. Minimum of would pick the smallest, Sum of adds them, and Average of averages them — none of which gives the single most valuable discount.

optionExplanations.A: The comparable monetary values make the maximum the largest eligible discount; the comparison basis is explicit in the scenario.
optionExplanations.B: The minimum selects the smallest saving, contradicting the requirement for the largest comparable discount value.
optionExplanations.C: Summing applies combined values rather than selecting one largest discount; the scenario requests a single value.
optionExplanations.D: An average describes the mean discount, not the one largest monetary value required by the scenario.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In an expression, how do you reference a field, and what does the symbol provide?

options.text: The dot operator ('.') references a field by name and lists the fields available in the current Case context
The at symbol ('@') references a field and lists all Access Roles
The hash symbol ('#') references a field and lists every Ruleset version
The slash ('/') references a field and lists the Case Stages

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall the symbol used to reference a field by name within a Pega expression.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Expressions reference fields by name using the dot operator ('.'), which lists the fields available in the current Case context; for a data-relationship field you prefix it with the property/list name. The other symbols are not used this way.

optionExplanations.A: The dot starts a field reference in the expression editor; relationship prefixes provide the context for nested values.
optionExplanations.B: The at symbol is not this field-reference syntax; the source’s field completion is not an Access Role list.
optionExplanations.C: The hash symbol is not the described field-reference operator and Ruleset versions are not the requested field suggestions.
optionExplanations.D: A slash is an arithmetic/path symbol in other contexts, not the editor’s described field-reference completion mechanism.

practiceQuiz.scenario: According to the reviewed Calculated values source, which group of Simple output field types does not support an expression calculation?

options.text: Email, Phone, and Picklist
Decimal, Currency, and Integer
Text, Date, and DateTime
Boolean, Text, and Currency

practiceQuiz.hint: Identify the three Simple field types that cannot have an expression calculation applied to them.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The source excludes Email, Phone and Picklist among Simple output types. This statement concerns the reviewed calculation configuration, not every use of those values as inputs or every future platform version.

optionExplanations.A: These are the reviewed exclusions for Simple output fields; do not confuse that restriction with whether values can be referenced as inputs.
optionExplanations.B: These numeric types are not the excluded group; they support the described numeric calculation approaches.
optionExplanations.C: The reviewed exclusion list is Email, Phone and Picklist rather than this offered text/date group.
optionExplanations.D: The reviewed exclusion list is not this Boolean, Text and Currency combination; consult the output-type distinction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An appraisal firm wants a comment like 'Appraiser 04795AD appraised Silver platter at a value of USD 350.' assembled from field values and static text. Which expression technique is this?

options.text: Concatenation — combine field references with static text in quotation marks using '+'
A Sum of function over the text fields
A Decision table that returns the full sentence
A Boolean AND expression that joins the fields

practiceQuiz.hint: Joining text + fields with quotes and '+'.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Concatenation assembles a text string by combining field references with static text (in quotation marks) joined with '+'; each reference is replaced with its current value at run time. A Sum function adds numbers, a Decision table returns a conditional result, and Boolean AND is a logical operation — none assembles the string.

optionExplanations.A: Joining literal text and current field references creates the required sentence without treating text as an aggregate of numbers.
optionExplanations.B: Numeric summation is not string assembly; these text and field segments need concatenation instead.
optionExplanations.C: A table can return a result, but the described assembly of current fields and literal fragments is concatenation.
optionExplanations.D: Boolean AND combines truth conditions rather than joining text fragments into the requested sentence.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Setting a loan's interest rate by evaluating the loan type against a set of logical tests is best implemented with which calculation type?

options.text: A Decision table — it evaluates fields with logical tests to return an appropriate result
A Function — Sum of returns the interest rate from the loan type
An Expression — multiply the loan type by a coefficient
Concatenation — join the loan type and a default rate

practiceQuiz.hint: Returning a result based on conditions tested against property values = Decision table.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A Decision table directly models loan-category-to-rate conditions. The offered Sum, loan-type multiplication and concatenation alternatives do not perform that lookup; this is not a claim that expressions cannot contain conditional logic or functions.

optionExplanations.A: The category-to-rate lookup is directly expressed by condition rows and outcomes, matching the stated selection requirement.
optionExplanations.B: Summing list values does not select a rate by loan category; it serves a different aggregation purpose.
optionExplanations.C: Multiplying a category label by a coefficient does not define the stated logical category-to-rate mapping.
optionExplanations.D: Joining category and rate as text does not evaluate the conditions required to select the appropriate numeric outcome.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A System Architect built a decision table in Dev Studio. What must be done so a Citizen Developer can reference it in App Studio?

options.text: Mark the decision table as a relevant record
Lock the Ruleset version that contains the table
Assign the table to an Access Role
Add the table to a Work Queue

practiceQuiz.hint: What must a developer do to a Dev Studio rule before citizen developers can reference it in App Studio?
practiceQuiz.rationale: To reuse a Dev Studio decision table in App Studio, you must mark it as a relevant record. Locking a Ruleset, assigning an Access Role, or adding it to a Work Queue do not expose the table to App Studio.

optionExplanations.A: Relevant designation makes the prepared table available in the App Studio selection context; permissions and applicability still matter separately.
optionExplanations.B: Ruleset locking concerns modification, not the relevant designation used for the calculated-field table selection list.
optionExplanations.C: An Access Role concerns authorization; it is not the reuse designation that makes this prepared table a relevant choice.
optionExplanations.D: A Work Queue holds Assignments; it is not where a Decision table is registered for calculation reuse.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Under what condition can a custom decision table be created directly in App Studio?

options.text: Only when the application is based on Constellation
Always — App Studio supports custom decision tables in every application
Only when the user has a System Architect Access Role
Only when the Ruleset is unlocked in Dev Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: Which UI architecture is required for creating custom decision tables directly in App Studio?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Only applications based on Constellation support creating custom decision tables directly in App Studio. Otherwise the table is built in Dev Studio and marked as a relevant record.

optionExplanations.A: The reviewed source limits direct custom-table creation in App Studio to Constellation; this is an architecture distinction.
optionExplanations.B: The reviewed source explicitly states a Constellation restriction, so universal availability contradicts that qualification.
optionExplanations.C: A user role alone does not replace the architecture prerequisite described for this custom creation feature.
optionExplanations.D: Unlocked Rule packaging alone does not replace the Constellation requirement for direct creation in App Studio.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining the calculation network to a developer building a loan application where interest rate depends on credit score, and monthly payment depends on the interest rate. Which TWO statements correctly describe how the calculation network works in Pega?

options.text: A calculated field can serve as the input to another calculation, creating dependent calculations
When a value changes, Pega updates all relevant dependent calculated fields automatically
The user must manually recalculate each dependent field after changing an input
Calculated fields are stored only in Access Roles, not in the data model

practiceQuiz.hint: Consider whether a calculated field can serve as input to another calculation — what happens then?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A calculated field can feed another calculation (A), and Pega's calculation network updates all relevant fields automatically when a value changes (B). C is wrong because the cascade is automatic, and D is wrong because calculated fields live in the Data model of a Case Type or data object, not in Access Roles.

optionExplanations.A: A configured calculated output can supply another calculation, which is how the dependency chain is formed.
optionExplanations.B: Input changes can update relevant dependent calculations through that configured network; unrelated fields are not implied.
optionExplanations.C: Manual recalculation of each dependency contradicts the automatic update behavior described for the configured calculation network.
optionExplanations.D: These fields belong to the Case or data-object model; Access Roles provide security context rather than this calculation storage.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is recommending a calculation approach for an insurance application where premium rate depends on age brackets and coverage type. Which TWO statements correctly describe when a Decision table is the appropriate calculation type?

options.text: A Decision table is appropriate when the calculated value depends on evaluating discrete input ranges or categories that map to specific output values
A row can test multiple input conditions, all of which must match for that row’s result under the described standard evaluation
A Decision table is the best choice when the calculation is a simple arithmetic formula such as price multiplied by quantity
Decision tables can return only numbers, never a supported text result

practiceQuiz.hint: Decision tables excel at condition-to-outcome mappings with multiple input columns — not simple formulas.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Tables express combinations of condition columns and results. The described evaluation considers rows in order, returns a complete match and uses otherwise when unmatched. Do not claim every possible data type is supported; match the result to its configured target.

optionExplanations.A: Discrete categories or ranges mapped to outcomes suit a table, especially when the result depends on combinations of inputs.
optionExplanations.B: The described standard evaluation tests all conditions in a row; a full row match returns its result.
optionExplanations.C: A simple product is directly expressed as an expression; a condition table adds unnecessary structure for that requirement.
optionExplanations.D: The numeric-only claim is too restrictive; the result must suit its target, and supported text outcomes are not excluded.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A developer is choosing between calculation types in App Studio for a set of derived fields in a loan application. Which TWO calculation types are directly available in App Studio for configuring a Calculated Value field?

options.text: Functions — basic aggregate choices such as Sum of or Maximum of over a list relationship
Decision tables — condition-outcome mappings that return a value based on evaluated field inputs
Machine Learning model — a predictive model trained on historical Case data to forecast the field value
Direct SQL query — a raw database query executed against the Pega schema to compute the field value

practiceQuiz.hint: App Studio offers three calculation types: Functions, Expressions, and Decision tables — no ML or SQL.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The reviewed App Studio calculation choices include basic aggregate Functions and Decision tables, as well as Expressions. ML prediction and direct SQL are not the named calculation types; callable expression functions are not the same as these aggregate choices.

optionExplanations.A: These aggregate choices are the Function category in the reviewed calculation list, distinct from arbitrary callable expression functions.
optionExplanations.B: This category selects outcomes from tested conditions and is one of the described App Studio calculation approaches.
optionExplanations.C: Prediction is not one of the three named field calculation types; invoking a model would need different configuration.
optionExplanations.D: Direct SQL is not a named App Studio calculated-field choice; database access is a separate platform concern.

quickRecap.value: Value derived from input fields; read-only; recalculates whenever an input changes. Created in the Data model of a Case Type or data object.
A calculated field can input another calculation; Pega cascades updates through all dependent calculated fields automatically.
Functions · Expressions · Decision tables (the App Studio calculation types).
Iterate over a list: Sum / Average / Maximum / Minimum of. Decimal, Currency, Integer only.
Reference fields via dot operator; +, −, ×, ÷, parens, Boolean AND/OR. Any Simple field except Email, Phone, Picklist. Text via concatenation.
Return a result from logical tests on fields (e.g. loan type → rate). Reuse a Dev Studio table by marking it a relevant record.
Custom decision tables in App Studio require a Constellation-based app.
